package: C finite synthetic sync/backup x86 load smoke review
reviewBinding: Working source snapshot identified by SHA256 manifest; helper and two runner hooks reviewed without source changes or execution.
independence: New helper authored by /root/backup and runner hooks by /root; reviewer did not author these changes.
scope: SyncBackupLoadSmoke.RunAsync and its evidence serialization/business verification helpers.
Canonical runner addition of one isolated LOAD_sync_backup_x86 scenario and existing fresh-directory/process timeout behavior.

workload.catalogUpdates: The same final500 product rows receive40 consecutive committed generations.

checks: Trusted QA login is reused in the synthetic database. Only fixture role grants are inserted, then the actor logs in again and demands PosSell/PosPay/DbBackup/CatalogImport. Worker demands bind the original session object/operator id.

Ready/start barriers coordinate one catalog worker and one actual backup worker. Native copy waits for first catalog commit and first issued public scan; the inspected online backup hook holds a source identity handle that permits catalog commits, not CatalogMutationGate.
Catalog counters advance only after successful ApplyAsync return and require500 applied/zero skipped/conflicts per page,40 run transactions,40 pages and released run guard.

Backup counter advances after CreateVerifiedAsync completes integrity/foreign-key validation and publication. Final source and reopened published snapshot require100k rows, unchanged sales/outbox, a uniform500-row generation, exact1000.125 stock and matching remote shadow.

Scans use the real PosView BarcodeBox bubbling input event/VM command and require exact cart count,quantity1,total and zero observed product SQL on UI. The first scan also invokes the public duplicate command while its guard is closed.

Payment work is explicitly preview-only: exact cash/card commands, receipt preview, confirm/cancel events and actual PaymentView rendering. It does not call the sale commit workflow; physical output callback throws and must remain unused.
All sample and native-interval list mutation/snapshot paths lock consistently. Private-memory maximum uses interlocked updates.

Budgeted asynchronous waits cancel their timeout tasks; finally opens start/scan barriers, cancels work/memory tokens and joins catalog,backup,memory workers before closing/disposal and restoring the operator session.
Synchronous native SQLite copy cannot be preempted mid-step; cleanup joins it and the canonical per-scenario process timeout remains the outer bound. The receipt states this limit explicitly.

Operation-active overlap is asserted separately from actual timestamped native-copy overlap. The fixture does not require or invent native overlap, network sync/scheduler execution or live convergence.

Worker peak assertions concern only the single fixture lanes and observed run-context semaphore. Private-memory peak is sampled at50ms plus UI endpoints afterseed/setup, not an exhaustive allocator peak.

Latency summaries retain first calls and use nearest-rank all-sample p50/p95/max. There are no performance pass thresholds; receipt flags performanceThresholdsApplied/liveBackendExecuted/integratedStabilityQualified/physicalOutputExecuted false.
Canonical runner supplies a new GUID temp directory and separate process for this scenario and propagates FAIL/nonzero/timeout. No existing assertions or timeouts were weakened by the hook.

Final canonical runner sets the process-local disabled loopback endpoint before launching visual and all functional scenario children, wraps the complete run in try/finally, and restores the previous environment value on success or failure. No persistent user/machine environment mutation is introduced.

resolvedInstrumentation.resolution: Count only false-to-true and true-to-false transitions with sawBusy, because repeated true notifications are not separate operations. Peak==1 and active==0 assertions remain.
Close each metric object with an explicit Append after AppendFormat and parse complete JSON grammar before publishing the receipt; numeric metrics and assertions remain.
Canonical runner now supplies the required disabled endpoint to visual and all scenarios and restores the previous process-local value in finally, making standalone CI execution self-contained.

executionPrerequisites: Helper requires x86 and WIN7POS_ADMIN_WEB_BASE_URL exactly http://127.0.0.1:9 before fixture work. The final canonical runner supplies the disabled endpoint to all child processes and restores its previous process environment in finally; direct helper invocations still fail closed if the endpoint differs.
Use the canonical fresh synthetic scenario directory. This review does not authorize running the harness on a live POS database.

validation.activity: Read-only source, two hook diffs and immediate backup/catalog/payment context.

rootReportedRuntimeEvidence.attribution: Root reports corrected runtime PASS with valid parsed JSON,40committed pages,1validated backup,24scans/24payment previews and worker peaks1. Reviewer did not run the scenario or infer a performance/live qualification PASS.

limits: One local finite fixture, not a live backend, network scheduler, sustained stability qualification or physical hardware acceptance.
Sampling can miss transient peaks and quantiles reflect the finite sample sizes, including a single backup.
45-second work budget starts after fixture setup; native copy/cleanup may extend past it and is governed by the outer process timeout.
